```hcl
provider "aws" {

  name            = "1.168.192.in-addr.arpa"  # Example IP address in reverse format
  type            = "PTR"
  ttl             = 300
  records         = ["host.example53.com"]
  depends_on      = [aws_route53_zone.reverse_zone]
}
```

   - The `records` attribute specifies the domain name that the PTR record should point to (`host.example53.com`).

### Description
This Terraform program sets up a blue/green deployment using AWS Route 53 to manage traffic between two environments that share a common RDS database. The program includes IAM roles and instance profiles, an RDS instance, a Route 53 hosted zone, and DNS records with health checks and a failover routing policy.

```hcl
provider "aws" {
  region = "us-west-2"  # Specify your desired AWS region
}

# IAM Role for EC2 instances
resource "aws_iam_role" "eb_ec2_role" {
  name = "eb_ec2_role"

  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Action = "sts:AssumeRole"
        Effect = "Allow"
        Principal = {
          Service = "ec2.amazonaws.com"
        }
      }
    ]
  })
}

# Instance Profile for EC2 instances
resource "aws_iam_instance_profile" "eb_ec2_profile" {
  name = "eb_ec2_profile"
  roles = [aws_iam_role.eb_ec2_role.name]
}

# Shared RDS Database
resource "aws_rds_instance" "myapp_db" {
  identifier              = "myapp-db"
  engine                  = "mysql"
  engine_version          = "8.0"
  instance_class          = "db.t3.micro"
  allocated_storage       = 20
  username                = "admin"
  password                = "securepassword"
  skip_final_snapshot     = true
  vpc_security_group_ids  = ["sg-0123456789abcdef0"]  # Replace with your security group ID
  db_subnet_group_name    = "myapp-db-subnet-group"   # Ensure this subnet group exists
}

# Route 53 Hosted Zone
resource "aws_route53_zone" "myapp_zone" {
  name = "myapp.example.com"
}

# DNS Record for Blue Environment
resource "aws_route53_record" "blue_record" {
  zone_id = aws_route53_zone.myapp_zone.zone_id
  name    = "blue.myapp.example.com"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300
  records = ["192.168.1.1"]  # Replace with the actual IP address of the blue environment
}

# DNS Record for Green Environment
resource "aws_route53_record" "green_record" {
  zone_id = aws_route53_zone.myapp_zone.zone_id
  name    = "green.myapp.example.com"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300
  records = ["192.168.1.2"]  # Replace with the actual IP address of the green environment
}

# Health Check for Blue Environment
resource "aws_route53_health_check" "blue_health_check" {
  fqdn                = aws_route53_record.blue_record.name
  port                = 80
  type                = "HTTP"
  resource_path       = "/"
  failure_threshold   = 3
  request_interval    = 30
  measure_latency     = true
  enable_sni          = true
  insufficient_data_health_status = "Healthy"
}

# Health Check for Green Environment
resource "aws_route53_health_check" "green_health_check" {
  fqdn                = aws_route53_record.green_record.name
  port                = 80
  type                = "HTTP"
  resource_path       = "/"
  failure_threshold   = 3
  request_interval    = 30
  measure_latency     = true
  enable_sni          = true
  insufficient_data_health_status = "Healthy"
}

# Failover Routing Policy Record
resource "aws_route53_record" "failover_record" {
  zone_id = aws_route53_zone.myapp_zone.zone_id
  name    = "myapp.example.com"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300

  health_check_ids = [
    aws_route53_health_check.blue_health_check.id,
    aws_route53_health_check.green_health_check.id
  ]

  set_identifier = "primary"
  routing_policy {
    type = "failover"
    failover {
      primary_routing_policy_type = "simple"
      secondary_routing_policy_type = "simple"
    }
  }

  records = ["192.168.1.1"]  # Primary record, will be replaced by health check logic
}
```

- Replace placeholder values such as IP addresses, security group IDs, and subnet group names with actual values from your AWS environment.
- Ensure that the IAM role (`eb_ec2_role`) has the necessary permissions for EC2 and RDS operations.
- The health checks are configured to monitor the availability of the respective environments via HTTP on port 80. Adjust the `fqdn`, `port`, and `resource_path` as needed for your application.
- The failover routing policy will automatically switch traffic to the healthy environment based on the health check results.

}

### Description
This Terraform program creates an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that forwards traffic to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The ALB has a listener that forwards traffic to the NLB's target group, which in turn forwards traffic to a backend target group. The program includes necessary security groups and listeners, and it ensures that the load balancers are properly configured to handle traffic.

### Terraform HCL Program

```hcl
provider "aws" {
  region = "us-west-2"
}

# Security Group for Application Load Balancer
resource "aws_security_group" "application_lb_sg" {
  name        = "application_lb_sg"
  description = "Security group for Application Load Balancer"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    from_port   = 80
    to_port     = 80
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }
}

# Application Load Balancer
resource "aws_lb" "application_load_balancer" {
  name               = "application-load-balancer"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "application"
  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.application_lb_sg.id]
  subnets            = var.subnets
}

# Target Group for Network Load Balancer
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "nlb_target_group" {
  name        = "nlb-target-group"
  port        = 443
  protocol    = "TCP"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id
  target_type = "ip"

  health_check {
    enabled             = true
    interval            = 30
    path                = "/"
    port                = "traffic-port"
    protocol            = "HTTP"
    timeout             = 5
    healthy_threshold   = 5
    unhealthy_threshold = 2
  }
}

# Listener for Application Load Balancer
resource "aws_lb_listener" "application_listener" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.application_load_balancer.arn
  port              = "80"
  protocol          = "HTTP"

  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.nlb_target_group.arn
  }
}

# Security Group for Network Load Balancer
resource "aws_security_group" "network_lb_sg" {
  name        = "network_lb_sg"
  description = "Security group for Network Load Balancer"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }
}

# Network Load Balancer
resource "aws_lb" "network_load_balancer" {
  name               = "network-load-balancer"
  internal           = false
  load_balancer_type = "network"
  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.network_lb_sg.id]
  subnets            = var.subnets
}

# Target Group for Backend Services
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "backend_target_group" {
  name        = "backend-target-group"
  port        = 80
  protocol    = "TCP"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id
  target_type = "instance"

  health_check {
    enabled             = true
    interval            = 30
    path                = "/"
    port                = "traffic-port"
    protocol            = "HTTP"
    timeout             = 5
    healthy_threshold   = 5
    unhealthy_threshold = 2
  }
}

# Listener for Network Load Balancer
resource "aws_lb_listener" "network_listener" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.network_load_balancer.arn
  port              = "443"
  protocol          = "TCP"

  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.backend_target_group.arn
  }
}

# Variables
variable "vpc_id" {
  description = "The ID of the VPC where the load balancers will be deployed"
  type        = string
}

variable "subnets" {
  description = "A list of subnet IDs where the load balancers will be deployed"
  type        = list(string)
  default     = []
}
```

- The security groups allow HTTP (port 80) for the Application Load Balancer and TCP (port 443) for the Network Load Balancer.
- Health checks are configured for both target groups to ensure proper routing of traffic.
- The `target_type` for the NLB target group is set to `ip`, and for the backend target group, it is set to `instance`. Adjust these settings based on your specific requirements.
